instructions: Pat the shrimp dry with paper towels. Transfer them to a bowl and toss with the olive oil and 3/4 tsp of the salt.
Mince the garlic and chop 2 tbsp of parsley leaves. Cut the lemon into wedges.
Heat a large cast iron or heavy skillet over high heat for about 3 minutes. It's ready when a drop of water vanishes the moment it lands.
Add half the shrimp in a single layer. Leave them alone for 2 minutes, until the shells are browned in spots. Stand back a little. They'll spatter.
Turn them and cook for 2 minutes. They're done when the meat is opaque and pink all the way through, with no gray, glassy spots.
Scatter half the garlic over the shrimp and cook for 30 seconds. Transfer them to a platter.
Cook the second half the same way, then add them to the platter.
Sprinkle the parsley and the last 1/4 tsp salt over the shrimp.
Taste one. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon.
method_notes: Every version cooks shell-on shrimp fast in a very hot dry or lightly oiled pan, salted, and finishes with lemon. Williams-Sonoma is the one followed here: oil and salt first, then garlic and parsley at the very end. Benidorm Seriously dips the shrimp in oil, lemon and salt and sears them in a dry pan, and Spain on a Fork cooks about 5 minutes total. The sources give 4 to 10 minutes of cooking; this one uses two batches of 4 minutes so the pan stays hot.
